findings.claim: Light/dark arguments swapped for .topic-meta-data h5 a: original $lightness 30% became dark-light-choose(70%, 30%) instead of (30%, 70%); light theme poster-name link fades from #646464 to #bdbdbd (contrast vs white ~5.9 -> ~1.9, below WCAG AA) and the dark theme gets the dim value.
findings.evidence: Diff '- scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)' -> '+ dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))'. Orchestrator ran the superpowers seat's pair-check script on the pinned patch: it prints exactly this line among 5 mismatches. No sass compiler; colour effect reasoned from scale-color semantics.
findings.reason: Three seats agree, mechanically verified; contradicts the commit's own rule (light value unchanged, dark = 100-X) and regresses the default light theme.

findings.evidence: Diff '- $lightness: 70%' -> '+ dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))'; desktop twin is (70%,30%). findings.reason: Three seats agree, mechanically verified; inverts intended muting in both themes.

findings.reason: Severity normalised to Important (superpowers and mattpocock Important, OCR Minor): unrequested light-theme visual change in a commit scoped to dark themes, with an accessibility drop.

findings.reason: Direct gap against the commit's stated intent; one-line change in a file the patch already touches.

findings.claim: The two-part dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, X%), scale-color($secondary, 100-X%)) expression is hand-copied 115 times across 32 files; a one-argument helper next to dark-light-choose/dark-light-diff would encode the 100-X rule once and would have prevented the 5 mismatches above.
findings.evidence: All 115 added lines follow the same shape (ponytail and mattpocock scripts); repo precedent: dark-light-diff at variables.scss:38-39. OCR noted the same but did not file it.
findings.reason: ponytail: advisory maintainability refactor touching 115 call sites; not a defect and would balloon the fix surface. Revisit as a follow-up refactor.

findings.claim: Comment still describes the old default 'scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)', now stale after the conversion.
findings.evidence: Orchestrator grep shows the comment line at common/base/discourse.scss:73.
findings.reason: ponytail: documentation-only, no runtime effect; outside the changed lines.

findings.claim: Several converted one-line rules gain a stray space before the closing brace ('...)); }' where the original was '...);}'), e.g. in desktop/topic-list.scss, desktop/queued-posts.scss:14 and desktop/topic-post.scss.
findings.evidence: Patch lines 502->503 and 529->530 change ');}' to '); }'. mattpocock seat said brace spacing was pre-existing; that holds for the opening '{color' but not for the new ' }', which the patch introduces.
findings.reason: ponytail: cosmetic whitespace only, no rendering effect; not covered by any lint config in the repo.

coverage: Files skipped: none - all 32 patched SCSS files covered by every seat (mechanical pairwise scripts plus manual reads at flagged sites). Axes that did not run: gate not run (benchmark mode: no dependency install, no project checks); no Sass compiler available, so no compiled CSS or rendered dark/light verification and all colour/contrast claims are reasoned from scale-color semantics with the default #222/#fff palette; no spec (judged against commit message); no SCSS lint config or style standards doc beyond CONTRIBUTING.md; no red tests or fix rounds (stopped after merge per benchmark override). Untracked harness dotfiles (.bashrc, .claude/, etc.) excluded from the pinned patch as not part of the PR.
